episodes.215323: With an elongated monsoon high spread west to east across the region, and modest low level moisture, afternoon thunderstorms were able to develop over the mountains of New Mexico August 18th. Two rounds of thunderstorms developed near the 2024 South Fork burn scar, moving over the scar just west of Ruidoso, NM. These storms dropped a quick 0.25 to 0.50 inches of rainfall over the burn scar, resulting in flash flooding impacts on portions of the Rio Ruidoso and Perk Canyon drainage basins. These storms moved westward off the burn scar, ending the threat by the late afternoon.

episodes.215957: Thunderstorms produced strong winds over the central bay of Green Bay during the afternoon hours on Tuesday (8/18).
episodes.216245: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued into the middle of August as a front remained in the vicinity of southeast Ohio on the 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. ||Daily showers and thunderstorms that pressed through the area during this time casted swaths of tree and power line damage across southeast Ohio. Additionally, 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, although some pockets of three to five inches were also observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts resulted in flooded roads and rises on creeks and streams in southeast Ohio. Impacts from heavier rain also included water rescues, some flooded structures, and river flooding on Duck Creek, Sunday Creek.
episodes.216246: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued in West Virginia as a front remained in the vicinity on August 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, though some pockets of three to five inches were observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts resulted in flooded roads across portions of West Virginia. Impacts from heavier rain also included water rescues, flooded structures, and river flooding on Clear Fork, Sand Run, Elk Twomile Creek, Tygart Valley River, West Fork River, and Middle Island Creek. Additionally, episodic rounds of strong thunderstorms produced during this timeframe resulted in more downed trees and power lines across the state. This occurred in locations that had already faced powerful storms earlier in the month, adding to the total of storm damage costs.
episodes.216574: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced several wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.216848: Clusters of storms tracked from north central to central South Dakota on the afternoon and evening of August 17th into the early morning of August 18th. A peak wind gust of 63 mph was recorded at the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 3 miles north of Gann Valley, with a 62 mph gust recorded on the Huron Remote Automated Weather Station (RAWS) in southeast Hand county. Higher winds, likely on the order of 70 to 80 mph, caused damage in northern Stanley county, with the roof blown off a shop and 15 power poles broken along South Dakota Highway 63.

episodes.217200: A line of thunderstorms ahead of a cold front tracked across southern Wisconsin from the afternoon into the evening hours.  Damaging winds occurred from numerous downbursts with one tornado occurring near Colgate in Washington County.
episodes.217260: A cold front slowly progressing through the UP coinciding with peak heating in the southern UP lead to isolated to scattered strong thunderstorms, which some were able to cause nickel size hail and cause tree damage in Menominee County on the 18th.
episodes.217310: During the afternoon and evening hours on August 18th, initially individual storm cells formed into a line in southeast Minnesota and west-central Wisconsin bringing severe hail and damaging wind gusts to the region.

episodes.217417: During the late evening hours of August 17, 2026, and continuing into the early morning hours of August 18, severe thunderstorms producing large hail and damaging wind gusts swept across eastern Nebraska. Thunderstorm initiation occurred along a southward-advancing cold front, with storm development further enhanced by strong low-level warm air advection atop the nose of an accelerating low-level jet (LLJ).||Convection initially developed as discrete supercells capable of producing very large hail, including ping-pong to tennis ball-sized hail up to 2.50 inches in diameter near Cedar Rapids, NE. As the night progressed, cell merger and upscale growth transformed the discrete convection into a linear Mesoscale Convective System (MCS). As this complex propagated across the area, it generated  severe wind gusts, resulting in measured wind gusts frequently ranging from 58 to 68 mph alongside scattered wind damage.
episodes.217602: During the late afternoon and early evening of Monday, August 17, 2026, an advancing cold front sparked isolated severe thunderstorms across north-central and northeastern Minnesota. Other than some isolated tree damage and sub-severe hail, storms remained below severe limits.
episodes.217817: On August 18th, scattered showers and storms developed over inland areas as the Atlantic sea breeze moved inland. This featured severe strong to isolated severe storms,  capable of wet microbursts, in the afternoon into evening. Several strong to severe storms that developed over Nassau and Duval County FL moved southeastward into nearshore Florida waters during the evening, resulting in strong wind gusts at the coast including the KSGJ AWOS.
episodes.217823: On August 18th, weak shortwave energy moved through the eastern periphery of the Heat Wave ridge over a moist and unstable airmass enhancing storms mainly over northeast and central Florida. Scattered showers and storms developed along the inland-moving sea breezes with stronger storms, capable of wet microbursts, pulsing along mesoscale boundary collisions in the afternoon into evening. On August 19-20, a frontal boundary stalled over southern Georgia as ���Heat Wave��� ridging built in from the west. Tropical moisture of 2+ inches of precipitable water remained south of the front, mainly over northeast Florida. Scattered showers and storms developed along the inland-moving sea breezes. The combination of high moisture, strong diurnal heating, and sea breeze/outflow interactions supported strong to severe storms capable of producing damaging winds, frequent lightning strikes and torrential downpours. Weak steering flow allowed for localized flooding. On August 22nd, lingering upper shortwaves ahead of the weakening frontal boundary in central Georgia triggered morning showers and isolated storms moving inland from the Gulf. Convection then spread east-northeastward through the day in the general southwest flow. A few stronger storms occurred along sea breeze boundary mergers in the late morning to early afternoon hours in north-central Florida.
episodes.217829: A cluster of storms tracked along a boundary from central Arkansas into north Mississippi during the afternoon hours of August 17th. A very unstable airmass north of the boundary provided the fuel for severe storms that produced damaging winds from east-central Arkansas to northeast Mississippi.
episodes.217917: Scattered thunderstorms developed in a more unstable airmass over central South Dakota and Nebraska and pushed eastward during the evening.  Storms encountered a more stable low-level environment, but an isolated storm produced a wind gust over 60 mph in the mid-James River valley.
episodes.217922: A thunderstorm developed along a backdoor cold frontal boundary across southwest Minnesota during the early evening of August 18. Shear and instability parameters were sufficient to produce marginally large hail.
episodes.218137: A line of thunderstorms ahead of a cold front tracked across southern Wisconsin from the afternoon into the evening hours. Damaging winds occurred from numerous downbursts to the lakeshore of Lake Michigan.
episodes.218266: The Black Hills saw two days of marginal severe weather, that brought wind and hail to the Black Hills and surrounding areas.
episodes.218281: Warm and unstable conditions led to isolated thunderstorm development on the evening of August 17.
episodes.218385: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over upstate South Carolina during the evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts over the foothills.
episodes.218492: A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved into western North Carolina from east Tennessee in advance of a cold front during the evening. Multiple embedded severe storms produced areas of damaging wind gusts across the mountains and foothills.
episodes.218530: Isolated thunderstorm development occurred along a boundary intersection across central Kansas that resulted in a severe wind and hail report.
episodes.218551: Onshore flow south of a slowly moving frontal boundary over the Deep South supported afternoon convection that produced a strong marine wind gust near Crystal River in Citrus County.
